cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-cheribsd/: **NO FAULT, AND NO REUSE.** The sequence completes with aliased=0: the stale pointer was followed, but the chunk it names was never handed to another allocation, because CheriBSD's libc holds a released chunk in QUARANTINE until the revoker has swept every capability to it. So the access reads only the dead object -- the exploitable half of a use-after-free, reading or writing SOMEONE ELSE'S object, did not happen. It is not a fault, because nothing forced a sweep between the free and the access: the stale capability still carried its tag, as the case was built to leave it. revocation control in the same boot: revocation=1 tag_after_sweep=0 reissued=1, then SIGPROT si_code 2 at the control's own probe, so the revoker demonstrably acts in this guest and a completion here is the mechanism's design, not an inactive mechanism. CONTRAST, measured in the sibling nested corpora: there the inner allocator reissues the storage at once and the stale pointer DOES read another object, because nothing reaches free(). Predicted before the run; the prediction held.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); cheribsd-abi, cheribsd-bounds and the revocation control all PASSED in the same boot.

title: a scratch table was released by a callee and then read by the next call
object: the VLCcode table from av_malloc_array, passed to two callees in turn
lifetime_ender: vlc_common_end(..., buf, flags, localbuf), which frees buf when it differs from localbuf
shape: ownership handed to a callee, then the same buffer used by the next call
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, with no pool or refstruct layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is `vlc_multi_gen(multi->table, vlc, nb_elems, j, nb_bits, buf, logctx)`.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions. CheriBSD measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-cheribsd/): NOT-REISSUED. Capstone measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-capstone/): spatial NOT CAUGHT, sublet CAUGHT. poisoncap-spatial measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-poisoncap-mode0/): NOT CAUGHT. poisoncap-protected measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-poisoncap-mode1/): NOT-REISSUED.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavcodec/vlc.c passes `buf` as vlc_common_end's last argument and frees it in the caller after vlc_multi_gen. The form passing `localbuf` and returning vlc_multi_gen directly is at 2e04d35c69e6^ and is absent from the pin.
nested_why: the object came straight from av_malloc/av_mallocz/av_malloc_array/av_realloc -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool, AVRefStructPool or other recycling layer between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../pool-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: the free is INSIDE a callee and conditional on `buf != localbuf`, so neither the free nor the later use is visible at the same place in the source -- the caller reads as a plain sequence of two helper calls. The fix passes `buf` as the callee's own fallback so it is not released there, and frees it in the caller after the second call.
